We need understand task. Original Question asks: A specific person who is founder of company whose online video games division released a video game in specific year 2000-2010, considered top-earning of all time at least until 2019, graduated from university founded 1930-1970. This person and spouse, up to 2019 had no children from marriage, made foundational gift for construction of a building part of larger complex. As of 2019, building scheduled to open 2018-2021 and part of specific university. As of 2023, which university was this building part of?

Task Skeleton requirements:
R1 Founder-company-game identification: person founder of company whose online video games division released a video game in year 2000-2010, top-earning until 2019.
R2 Founder education: graduated from university founded 1930-1970.
R3 Marriage and childlessness: person and spouse, up to 2019, no children from marriage.
R4 Gift-funded building: person and spouse made foundational gift for construction of building part of larger complex.
R5 Planned opening and affiliation: As of 2019, building scheduled to open 2018-2021, and part of a specific university.
R6 Requested building university: As of 2023, which university was this building a part of?

Verified Claims:
C1 Kwon Hyuk-bin founded Smilegate in 2002; Smilegate maker of Crossfire, Lost Ark, other games.
C2 Kwon Hyuk-bin holds electrical engineering degree from Sogang University.
C3 As of June 2025, Kwon Hyuk-bin was listed as separated and having 2 children.
C4 Ding Lei founded NetEase June 1997, founder/CEO; NetEase online/mobile games, fortune from video games including Fantasy Westward Journey.
C5 Ding Lei earned degree in communication technology from University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; at time of 2019 article, married but without children.

Need assess each requirement. The claims are about two possible people: Kwon Hyuk-bin (Smilegate founder) and Ding Lei (NetEase founder). The original question likely points to Ding Lei? Let's see: Founder of company whose online video games division released a video game in 2000-2010 top-earning until 2019. NetEase? Ding Lei founded NetEase. NetEase online games division released Fantasy Westward Journey in 2003? It was top-earning? Ding Lei graduated from UESTC? Founded? UESTC founded 1956 (between 1930-1970). He married but no children up to 2019. Made gift with spouse for building? Possibly "Ding Lei and his wife made a donation to build a building at University of Electronic Science and Technology of China"? The question asks building part of university as of 2023. Could be Ding Lei? Let's recall: Ding Lei (William Ding) donated to University of Electronic Science and Technology of China? There is "Ding Lei Building" or "Ding Lei and his wife donated 100 million yuan to build the Ding Lei Building (?) at UESTC"? Hmm. But we must not use outside knowledge beyond claims. Need judge based only on claims. 

Task requirements:
R1 requires founder of a company whose online video games division released a video game in specific year 2000-2010, at least until 2019 considered top-earning games of all time. Claims: C4 says Ding Lei founded NetEase in 1997; NetEase online/mobile games business; fortune from video games including Fantasy Westward Journey. This establishes founder of company in online games and a game Fantasy Westward Journey, but does not state release year between 2000-2010 nor considered top-earning until 2019. C1 says Kwon founded Smilegate in 2002; maker of Crossfire, Lost Ark, etc. Does not state online video games division released game in year 2000-2010? Smilegate founded 2002, maybe Crossfire released 2007, but claim doesn't say release year or top-earning until 2019. C4 mentions Fantasy Westward Journey but no year/top-earning. So R1 partially? It establishes founder-company-game identification partially: founder of company whose online games division released a video game? C4: Ding Lei founded NetEase, an online and mobile games business, and fortune came largely from video games including Fantasy Westward Journey. That implies NetEase released/owned a video game. But not "online video games division released" nor specific year 2000-2010 nor top-earning until 2019. C1: Kwon founded Smilegate in 2002; maker of Crossfire, Lost Ark, other games. It establishes founder of company that makes games. Not specific year/top-earning. So at least one substantive material part? R1 is complex: founder of company whose online video games division released a video game in specific year between 2000-2010, which at least until 2019 considered one of top-earning games of all time. The claims establish "founder of company (Smilegate/NetEase) that makes online games" and "a game (Fantasy Westward Journey)" but do not establish release year in range, nor top-earning until 2019. So partially_supported. Could it be unsupported? Material parts: founder-company-game identification. C4 gives founder of NetEase, online games business, and video game Fantasy Westward Journey. So yes substantive part: person is founder of company with online games/video games, and game exists. But the specific year and top-earning status are unsupported. So partial.

R2: Founder education: graduated from a university founded between 1930 and 1970. Claims: C2 Kwon Hyuk-bin holds electrical engineering degree from Sogang University. Does not state university founded between 1930-1970. Sogang University founded 1960 (outside? actually 1960, between). But claim doesn't mention founding date. C5 Ding Lei earned degree from University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; no founding date. So no claim establishes university founded between 1930 and 1970. It establishes graduation from a university, but not the founding date condition. So partially_supported? Requirement: "graduated from a university founded between 1930 and 1970." Material parts: graduated from a university AND that university founded between 1930-1970. Claims establish graduation from universities (C2, C5). The founding date condition remains unsupported. Thus partially_supported. Could be fully? No. Unsupported? No, because graduation from university is a substantive part. But wait requirement specifically "graduated from a university founded between 1930 and 1970" — the core is university's founding date? It includes graduation from a university. So partial.

R3: Marriage and childlessness: person and spouse, up to 2019, had no children from marriage. Claims: C5 Ding Lei at time of 2019 article, married but without children. This establishes marriage and no children up to 2019 (for Ding Lei). However "from the marriage" maybe same. C3 Kwon as of June 2025 separated and having 2 children—does not support no children up to 2019? It contradicts? It says as of 2025 separated and 2 children. It doesn't say up to 2019 no children. So C5 fully supports for Ding Lei. Does R3 require specific person? It's tied to the person from R1. But we don't know if R1 person is Ding Lei or Kwon. The claims provide C5 for Ding Lei. If the person is Ding Lei, R3 fully supported. But we need determine support for requirement as stated. It says "This person and their spouse, who, up to 2019, had no children from the marriage" referring to specific person. C5 says Ding Lei at time of 2019 article married but without children. C3 says Kwon had separated and 2 children as of 2025. Does C5 fully support R3? It establishes for Ding Lei. But is Ding Lei the person identified by R1? R1 not fully supported. However the requirement is about "this person". We can use claims to support it if they establish a person matching? But R1 not established. The rules: A Claim supports a Requirement only when the Claim materially establishes part of what that Requirement requires. R3 requires "This person and their spouse ...". It presupposes the person. C5 provides that Ding Lei was married but without children at time of 2019 article. Does it establish "up to 2019 had no children from marriage"? Yes for Ding Lei. But is Ding Lei "this person"? The claims include C4 identifying Ding Lei as founder of NetEase, which may be the person from R1. C5 links to same Ding Lei. So collectively C4 and C5 establish that Ding Lei (founder of NetEase) was married but no children up to 2019. However R1's game/year/top-earning not fully established. But for R3, the person reference could be resolved to Ding Lei via C4/C5. The requirement does not require the full R1 conditions; it just requires marriage/childlessness for that person. If C5 says Ding Lei married but without children at time of 2019 article, then R3 fully supported? The phrase "up to 2019" means until 2019. "At the time of the 2019 article, he was married but without children." That indicates as of 2019 no children. It doesn't explicitly say from the marriage, but "married but without children" implies no children in marriage? Could be no children at all. Probably sufficient. So R3 fully_supported by C5. But what about C3 for Kwon? It says as of 2025 separated and 2 children. That doesn't affect Ding Lei. If the person could be Kwon, then R3 unsupported. But the claims include both. The task likely expects using C5 for Ding Lei. However we must be careful: R3 says "This person and their spouse, who, up to 2019, had no children from the marriage". C5 says "at the time of the 2019 article, he was married but without children." That fully supports. So R3 fully_supported with C5.

R4: Gift-funded building: person and spouse made a foundational gift for construction of a building part of larger complex. Claims: none mention gift or building. C3/C5 mention marriage/spouse but no gift. So unsupported. supported_by empty.

R5: Planned opening and affiliation: As of 2019, building scheduled to open 2018-2021, and part of specific university. Claims: none mention building scheduled opening or university affiliation. Unsupported. Empty.

R6: Requested building university: As of 2023, which university was this building a part of? This is the question asking answer. No claim provides building's university. Unsupported. Empty.

Need decide statuses for R1, R2. R1 partially_supported? R2 partially_supported. R3 fully_supported? R4 unsupported, R5 unsupported, R6 unsupported.

Let's examine if R1 might be unsupported because no claim establishes "specific year between 2000 and 2010" nor "top-earning until 2019". But it does establish founder-company-game identification in part: C4: Ding Lei founded NetEase, online and mobile games business, fortune from video games including Fantasy Westward Journey. "founder of a company whose online video games division released a video game" — NetEase is online games business, but "division" not explicit. C1: Kwon founded Smilegate, maker of Crossfire, Lost Ark. Smilegate is game company. But "online video games division released a video game in specific year" not established. The requirement's label is "Founder-company-game identification". It includes the entire phrase. The material parts: (a) person is founder of company; (b) company's online video games division released a video game in a specific year between 2000 and 2010; (c) that game was considered one of top-earning games of all time at least until 2019. Claims establish (a) for Ding Lei and Kwon, and existence of games. They do not establish (b) specific year in range or (c) top-earning. So partially supported. But if we interpret "specific year between 2000 and 2010" as a condition that must be met, and it's not, then only (a) and game existence are supported. Still partial.

R2: "graduated from a university founded between 1930 and 1970." Claims establish graduation from a university (C2, C5). They do not establish founding date. So partial.

R3: "This person and their spouse, who, up to 2019, had no children from the marriage." C5 establishes for Ding Lei married but without children at time of 2019 article. Does it establish spouse? "he was married" implies spouse. "without children" likely no children from marriage. So fully supported. If we need "up to 2019" meaning continuously until 2019, C5 only at time of 2019 article. But "at the time of the 2019 article" means as of 2019. It doesn't say before 2019, but "up to 2019" might mean until 2019. The claim "at the time of the 2019 article, he was married but without children" establishes no children as of 2019, which covers up to that point? It doesn't explicitly say no children before, but if he was without children at that time, likely no children at that time. The requirement "up to 2019, had no children" could be interpreted as until 2019 they had no children. A single point at 2019 might not establish the entire interval up to 2019. But typically "as of 2019, had no children" is enough for "up to 2019 had no children" in these tasks. Could be fully_supported. Alternatively, partially_supported if "up to 2019" requires continuous childlessness and claim only says at 2019. But I think fully.

R4: no claim. Unsupported.

R5: no claim. Unsupported.

R6: no claim. Unsupported.
